OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly two repo paths: factory/graphs.py (edit) and tests/test_comms_invariant_lint.py (create). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or stage anything else. Never touch .git, never commit, never push, never run git add. Never modify any charter.yaml, anything under runbooks/, or CLAUDE.md (governance, human-only). Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. No network access needed or allowed.

READ FIRST (read-only, for conventions): factory/graphs.py (validate_subgraph at ~line 66, validate_subgraphs at ~124, check_traceability at ~134), loopfactory.py cmd_validate at ~line 74 (to see which functions `validate` actually calls), departments/podcast/subgraphs.json and departments/social/subgraphs.json (current node shapes), one existing test under tests/ for style.

FEATURE BRIEF — the comms-loop-invariant lint guard: this factory recently shipped a department that sent 57 outreach asks, received 16 replies, and harvested 0, because nothing required an outbound ask to have a return path. Add a deterministic lint rule to the subgraph validation path that loopfactory.py validate executes: any node whose definition carries "emits_ask": true MUST also declare "return_path" (non-empty string naming the component that reads the answers) and "return_sla_hours" (number > 0). A violating node produces a clear error string naming the node id and the missing field(s), flowing into the same error list the existing validators use. Nodes WITHOUT emits_ask are completely unaffected — the guard must be purely additive so both existing departments (podcast, social) still validate clean. Unknown extra fields on nodes must not crash the guard.

TESTS (create tests/test_comms_invariant_lint.py, following existing test style): (1) RED case — a minimal subgraph containing a node with emits_ask true and no return_path/return_sla_hours returns errors naming the node and both missing fields; (2) GREEN case — same node with both fields present returns no comms errors; (3) vacuous case — a subgraph with no emits_ask nodes returns no comms errors; (4) bad-value case — return_sla_hours of 0 or negative errors.

HOW TO RUN, from the repo root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_comms_invariant_lint.py -q · python3 loopfactory.py validate --name podcast · python3 loopfactory.py validate --name social · PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/ -q (the whole suite must stay green).

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the two owned files changed/created in the repo, plus ./notes.md in the scratch dir listing: what you read for conventions, exactly where the guard hooks into the validate flow, which commands you ran and their results, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: boring and local to existing patterns; no new dependencies; no edits outside the two owned paths even to fix an unrelated failure (report it in notes.md instead); if the validate flow is not where the READ FIRST pointers suggest, follow the real call path from loopfactory.py and say so in notes.md.
tasks.verified: new lint tests pass including the RED case, guard strings present in graphs.py, podcast and social validate stay clean, full suite green, no files touched outside ownership, charter untouched.

You are a repo feature worker editing a real repository: /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory. Your current working directory is a scratch task directory; use it only for ./notes.md.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly: departments/podcast/runtime/comms_reconcile_sensor.py (create), tests/test_comms_reconcile_sensor.py (create), tests/fixtures/comms_reconcile/ (create, fixture JSONs). Nothing else. Never touch .git, never commit, never push. Never modify charter.yaml, runbooks/, CLAUDE.md, or any existing file. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. The sensor and your work are strictly LOCAL and READ-ONLY toward the world: no network imports (no requests/urllib usage/smtplib/googleapiclient), no sends, no writes outside owned paths.

READ FIRST (read-only, for conventions): departments/podcast/runtime/hopper_sensor.py and departments/podcast/runtime/pipeline_sensor.py (the sensor idiom in this codebase: argparse CLI, pure functions, JSON out), departments/podcast/runtime/README.md if present. You MAY read /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/_loop_receipts/referral-touch-20260803.json READ-ONLY to learn the real tracker-report schema (schema name obe.referral-touch-report.v1) — but you must NOT copy any name, email, or contact-identifying value out of it; your fixtures are fully synthetic with counts only.

FEATURE BRIEF — the comms reconcile sensor. Context: the podcast estate asks past guests for referrals. A tracker report counts outbound referral touches and inbound replies; a referral ledger (REFERRALS.json, schema referral-ledger-v1) holds harvested referrals in its referrals[] array. Recently the truth was 57 asked, 16 replied, 0 harvested — an open loop nothing detected. Build a standalone, pure, deterministic sensor that reads BOTH files and applies the open-loop invariant: if an upstream count is > 0 and the next count downstream is 0, emit a finding.

CLI CONTRACT (the check depends on this exactly): python3 departments/podcast/runtime/comms_reconcile_sensor.py --tracker PATH --ledger PATH [--sla-hours N] prints to stdout a single JSON object {"findings": [...]} and exits 0 whenever it ran (findings are data, not errors; a malformed input file IS an error finding with code "input_unreadable", still exit 0). Each open-loop finding must include at least: code="open_loop", chain (e.g. "replied->harvested"), asked (int), replied (int), harvested (int), severity ("warn" or "action"), and a human-readable detail sentence. Derive asked/replied from the tracker report's counts and harvested from len(referrals[]) in the ledger. Handle both key spellings you find in the real tracker schema gracefully; if a count is absent, treat it as unknown and emit code="count_missing" rather than assuming zero (unmeasured is never zero in this codebase).

FIXTURES (all synthetic): tests/fixtures/comms_reconcile/tracker_57_16_0.json (57 outbound touches, 16 inbound replies), referrals_empty.json (valid referral-ledger-v1 with referrals: []), tracker_healthy.json + referrals_present.json (a healthy pair where replies exist AND referrals[] is non-empty so NO open_loop fires). No real names, no real email domains.

TESTS (tests/test_comms_reconcile_sensor.py): (1) the 57/16/0 pair yields exactly one open_loop finding with replied=16, harvested=0; (2) the healthy pair yields no open_loop; (3) missing count key yields count_missing, not a zero assumption; (4) unreadable ledger path yields input_unreadable, exit 0.

HOW TO RUN, from repo root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_comms_reconcile_sensor.py -q · then the CLI against your fixtures as in the contract above.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the owned files, plus ./notes.md: what you read, the real tracker-schema keys you bound to (keys only, no values), commands run and results, assumptions.

HARD RULES: standard library only; no wiring into the daily chain or manager (that is a separate governed map change); boring, small, matching the sibling sensors' style.
tasks.verified: sensor tests pass, CLI emits open_loop with replied=16/harvested=0 on the synthetic 57/16/0 fixture, no false positive on the healthy pair, no network imports, fixtures contain no real contact data, scope and governance clean.
